paper: Huang, Shao & Tsymbal, arXiv:2202.11348, Ferroelectric control of magnetic skyrmions in 2D vdW heterostructures
verdict_note: Core mechanism (DMI-controlled skyrmion creation/annihilation via FE switching; chirality tied to sign(D)) fully reproduced; absolute skyrmion diameter off ~2-3x due to unknown exchange stiffness A.

open_questions.question: What is the paper's actual exchange stiffness A (only shown in Fig.4), and does using it collapse our ~40 nm diameter onto the reported ~12 nm?
open_questions.why_heavy: Skyrmion size and the critical DMI both scale as sqrt(A). A is the single unknown separating our correct threshold/trend from an absolute-size match. It lives only in a figure image, so recovering it requires either digitizing Fig.4, reproducing the DFT-fitted Heisenberg J -> A conversion, or an author query. Without it the absolute-size gap cannot be closed.
open_questions.compute_needed: Fig.4 image digitization + DFT exchange-parameter fit (uicgpu A100), OR author correspondence.

open_questions.question: Does rebuilding on the true Fe honeycomb lattice (rather than the square-lattice approximation) change the geometric DMI prefactor enough to shift D_c relative to the paper's D values?
open_questions.why_heavy: The interfacial-DMI bond geometry differs between square and honeycomb lattices; the honeycomb has a different coordination and bond-direction set, altering the effective micromagnetic D and thus D_c=(4/pi)sqrt(AK). Quantifying this requires reimplementing the full honeycomb bond DMI and re-relaxing, then comparing D_c on both lattices.
open_questions.compute_needed: Honeycomb-lattice micromagnetic relaxer (CPU, nuc13/spark) — moderate rebuild of the energy/effective-field kernel.

open_questions.question: Can we reproduce the DFT-computed FE-switchable DMI values (0.28 vs 0.06 mJ/m^2 bilayer; 0.22 vs -0.24 trilayer) from first principles, rather than taking them as inputs?
open_questions.why_heavy: This is the paper's actual first-principles result — the interfacial DMI as a function of In2Se3 polarization state, computed via the constrained-spin / four-state DFT method on the Fe3GeTe2/In2Se3 supercell with SOC. It requires a large relativistic DFT calculation and the D_up ~= D_upup + D_down relation check; it is the microscopic origin of everything the micromagnetics consumes.
open_questions.compute_needed: Relativistic DFT+SOC on Fe3GeTe2/In2Se3 hetero-supercell (uicgpu A100 or ALCF); four-state / constrained-moment DMI extraction.

open_questions.question: Are the trilayer skyrmions (D=0.22, |D|=0.24 mJ/m^2), which sit just below our analytic D_c=0.255, thermodynamically stable or merely metastable from the seed?
open_questions.why_heavy: Our seeded overdamped relaxation finds skyrmions at D just below D_c, consistent with Eq.6 giving a small finite R near threshold, but a seeded relaxation cannot distinguish a true energy minimum from a long-lived metastable state. Settling this requires energy-barrier / GNEB nudged-elastic-band calculations of the skyrmion vs uniform-FM states across the D sweep.
open_questions.compute_needed: GNEB / minimum-energy-path micromagnetics across D (CPU-parallel sweep, nuc13 or Crux).

open_questions.question: Does a full atomistic spin-dynamics run with the paper's true anisotropy caveat (DFT MAE 8.57 MJ/m^3 vs adopted 0.04 MJ/m^3) reproduce the ~0.03 nm 'no skyrmion' regime and the ~100 nm experimental regime as the paper's Eq.6 predicts?
open_questions.why_heavy: The paper's honest tension is that its own DFT anisotropy is 200x too large for any observable skyrmion, forcing an adopted K. Mapping the full R(K) curve from Eq.6 and confirming both limits (0.03 nm at DFT-K, ~100 nm at experimental-K~0.008 MJ/m^3) tests whether the adopted K=0.04 is the right qualitative compromise and quantifies the model's sensitivity to the least-constrained parameter.
open_questions.compute_needed: Parameter sweep over K in the existing relaxer (cheap, spark/nuc13) + Eq.6 analytic curve.

next_steps: Digitize Fig.4 (or query authors) to recover A; re-run the relaxer with the true A and check the ~12 nm diameter (closes Q1, the main size gap).
Extend the square-lattice kernel to the Fe honeycomb and recompute D_c to bound the geometric-prefactor error (Q2).
Stand up a relativistic DFT+SOC hetero-supercell calc to reproduce the FE-switchable DMI values from first principles (Q3).
Add a GNEB minimum-energy-path check to confirm stability vs metastability of the near-threshold trilayer skyrmions (Q4).
Sweep K and overlay Eq.6 to reproduce the paper's anisotropy tension across the 0.03 nm / 12 nm / 100 nm regimes (Q5).
